newsitem.title: UK: GOVIA preferred bidder for UK's Thameslink.
newsitem.headline: GOVIA preferred bidder for UK's Thameslink.

text.p: Britain's rail franchising agency said on Thursday it named a joint venture formed by Go-Ahead Group Plc and France's VIA-GTI as the preferred bidder for the Thameslink passenger rail service.
Britain's Office of Passenger Rail Franchising (Opraf) said in a statement that it expected a formal award announcement giving details to be released soon.
The Anglo-French venture, called GOVIA, is 65 percent owned by Go-Ahead and 35 percent by VIA-GTI.
Go-Ahead's shares jumped 28p to 505 by 1550 GMT.
The Thameslink rail franchise runs to Luton and Gatwick airports through the financial district of London and is seen as having great potential as a fast-link to these major UK airports.
Go-Ahead has already won the Thames rail franchise and GOVIA had been shortlisted for Thameslink, as well as ScotRail and Regional Railways North East.
Go-Ahead, a bus and rail operator, has around eight percent of the UK bus market, with fleets running in London, Oxford and the north east of England.
The group has been among a number of UK bus companies to move into rail, fuelling growth in earnings.
